invariantAllocations.invariant: Program Kit-owned implementation C# satisfies the current private repository source-quality policy.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing private PKCS analyzer and build spine already enforce Program Kit repository source structure and behavioral rules.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Operation, host projection, bridge, capability, CLI, and provider projects preserve approved reference direction and package topology.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing build spine, explicit solution graph, locked restore, and architecture conformance tests own static dependency enforcement.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Runtime packages do not embed or reference agent-session capability content except through exact inert distribution manifests.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Project/package reference conformance and package-layout tests can prove the static isolation boundary; provider activation cannot.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Application and Program Kit consumer proofs use exact packages and installed closure without repository/source/build-output coupling.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Package provenance, source mapping, generated hosts, bundle materialization, and absence of source knowledge require isolated filesystem and process conformance.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Operation catalogs, exposure bindings, Console introspection, MCP tools, schemas, results, and failures preserve exact identity and contract semantics.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Cross-artifact bytes, protocol behavior, generated-host execution, and application outputs cannot be proven by a C# analyzer.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Bundles, operation bindings, knowledge closure, content-addressed storage, provider adapters, ownership locks, flat catalogs, refresh, update, and cold-session guidance conform to exact contracts.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Byte graphs, provider discovery, application-authored semantics, and cross-session behavior require schema, integration, and genuine provider evidence.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Tool registration, capability initialization, provider trust/permission, and invocation remain separate and no autonomous loop exists.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Configuration mutation, process start, provider prompts, and absence of automatic behavior are observable process properties rather than compiler properties.

rationale: The existing private Program Kit C# gate remains exactly compatible with Program Kit-owned implementation. Current committed main additionally verifies reusable gate package manifests against Git-normalized index bytes. No new analyzer, gate extension, generated-source attachment, or consumer attachment is justified; protocol, package-only, capability, provider, and cold-session behavior remain executable proof.
residualRisks: The private Program Kit gate remains a repository-specific source-policy monolith with an MSBuild trust boundary.

Static analysis cannot prove package-only construction, exact runtime bytes, protocol negotiation, provider trust or permissions, capability triggering, knowledge closure use, cold-session isolation, or genuine external provider evidence.
Application semantic correctness remains publisher-owned and outside Program Kit static proof.
nonStaticClaims: Schema projection, generated Console introspection, OpenAPI binding, MCP modern/legacy negotiation, tools/list/call, canonical results, timeout, cancellation, concurrency, registration, capability lifecycle, catalog regeneration, and removal require dedicated executable tests.
Genuine Codex and Claude Code cold-session evidence and human review remain authoritative for provider-native capability/tool selection, trust, permission, and non-autonomous behavior.
Publisher attestation, not Program Kit conformance, remains authoritative for application workflow semantics.
